challenges.name: arrays-readonly-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: sort() and readonly arrays
challenges.description: Work out what the default sort does to numbers, then pick what a function may do with a readonly array parameter.

questions.explanation: Without a compare function, sort converts every element to a string and sorts the strings by UTF-16 code units: "12000" < "125000" < "180000" < "38000" < "65000", so the array becomes [12000, 125000, 180000, 38000, 65000]. The first element happens to be the smallest, but the last one is 65000, not 180000. TypeScript accepts sort() without arguments on number[] - the compare function is optional - so there is no compile error. Sort numbers with (a, b) => a - b.

options.text: Nothing: tsc reports that sort() on a number[] needs a compare function.

questions.question: Inside function f(items: readonly Product[]), with interface Product { sku: string; price: number }, which lines compile with tsc --strict? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: toSorted returns a new array and leaves items alone, so it exists on readonly arrays. [...items] copies the elements into a new, mutable array, which you may sort. items[0].price = 0 compiles too: readonly Product[] only forbids changing the array (adding, removing, reordering elements); the Product objects inside are still mutable unless their properties are readonly. push and reverse change the array, so they do not exist on readonly Product[] (error TS2339). Assigning items to a Product[] variable would let you mutate it through the new name, so it is error TS4104.

options.text: const byPrice = items.toSorted((a, b) => a.price - b.price);

challenges.name: fix-best-sellers-sort
challenges.title: Fix the best-sellers widget that reorders the catalog
challenges.description: The Chợ Sớm home page shows the best sellers and a price range, computed from the catalog that every category page shares. The widget sorted the catalog in place, so the category pages showed products by sales, and the default sort put 65.000 đ above 180.000 đ. Now that the catalog is a readonly Product[], the starter does not compile. Fix bestSellers (most sold first, ties by sku, at most n products) and priceRange (lowest and highest price as a tuple) without changing the catalog. The test runner reads n and the catalog as JSON and prints the best sellers, the price range and the catalog order.
